name: Phuong
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 8 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Wallace, Judith M. 1969. Katu phonemes. Mon-Khmer Studies 3: 64-73. (Primary phonological description of Katu, Quảng Nam, Vietnam: based on the Low Katu of Anđiềm with reference to the Low Katu of Phúhòa and the High Katu dialect of Chuah, sec. 4.2.) Corroborated by Costello, Nancy A. 1991. Nôôq paraaq Katu = Katu dictionary: Katu-Vietnamese-English. Tủ sách ngôn-ngữ dân-tộc thiểu-số Việt-Nam 5(2). Manila: SIL Thailand Group, front matter 'Orthography' > 'Word Structure and Phoneme Distribution' (Glottolog ref 147966, the Glottolog's most extensive description for phuo1238; hh.bib language code 'Eastern Katu [ktv], High Katu = Phuong [phg]').
catalog_locator: Wallace 1969 p. 69, sec. 3 'Word Structure and phoneme Distribution' (stress statement); p. 71 (presyllable vowels v₂, v₃ 'usually actualize as an unstressed [ə]'; MS = C₁V±C₄ or C₂C₃V±C₄; four-syllable maximum, tapasaruum, tapaglâk); p. 64 (identity: 'This study is based on the Low Katu dialect spoken in Anđiềm (SW of Đànẵng) with references to the Low Katu dialect of Phúhòa (W of Đànẵng) and the High katu dialect of Chuah (near Laos border).'); p. 72 sec. 4.2 'Chuah dialect' (High Katu, same phonemic inventory, no stress difference stated). Scan (originhttps://sealang.net/archives/mks/pdf/3:15-page scan, article = file pages 4-13). Secondary: Costello 1991 front matter ('Orthography' > 'Word Structure and Phoneme Distribution'; 'Dialects' page).
catalog_quote: The katu word has a main syllable which can be precedeŋ by one, two, or three presyllables. The word can be symbolized as c₃v/c₂v/c₁v/ MS. (Lower case is used for presyllable symbols, upper case for main syllable symbols.) The main syllable always receives the major stress. c₃v and c₂v are always affixes, and c₁v sometimes is. The vowel position in all presyllables is filled by /a/. ... [p. 71] v₂ and v₃ usually actualize as an unstressed [ə]. ... The Main syllable (MS) can occur as C₁V±C₄ or as C₂C₃V±C₄. ... No consonant clusters have been found in four-syllable words. ... Examples of maximum word expansion: tapasaruum « cause each other to fall », tapaglâk « cause each other to carry ». ... [p. 72, 4.2 Chuah dialect:] The Chuah dialect is considered a High Katu dialect and has approximately 75% general vocabulary correspondence with the Anđiềm Low Katu dialect. They are partly mutualy intelligiblle. In all differences between the Phúhòa and Anđiềm dialects discussed above, Chuah matches Anđiềm. The Chuah phonemic inventory is the same as the other dialects, but with a few distribution differences.
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: The Katu word has a main syllable which can be preceded by one, two or three presyllables. The word can be symbolised as CV3/CV2/CV1/MS. CV3 and CV2 are always affixes, whereas CV1 is rarely an affix. Presyllables are always unstressed. The main syllable MS can be symbolised as CV±C or CCV.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Katu words are sesquisyllabic: a main syllable (CV±C or CCV) optionally preceded by up to three presyllables (CV3/CV2/CV1), and the presyllables are always unstressed, so word prominence falls on the final, main syllable. Stress is therefore fixed on the last (main) syllable; it is a phonotactic/structural property rather than a contrastive one.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the same statement is given for all three dialects the dictionary covers (An-Diem, Phu-Hoa, High Katu).
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word (dictionary entries, i.e. citation forms); nothing said about phrase-level prominence. The statement covers the Katu of Quang Nam (Low Katu An-Diem and Phu-Hoa, High Katu); its application to Phuong rests on Glottolog's identification High Katu = Phuong [phg].
new_statements.identity_note: No description written for "Phuong" as such exists. Glottolog 5.3 keeps phuo1238/phg as a language (Katuic > Katu; alt names Huu River Vân Kiêu, Phuang, Phuong Catang; AES 6a Vigorous, ethnic group Cơ Tu) but its entire bibliography for phg is Costello's Katu dictionary (1991) and Katu vocabulary (1971), tagged in hh.bib `language code = {Eastern Katu [ktv], High Katu = Phuong [phg]}`; Wikipedia likewise glosses Phuong as "High Katu", and Glottolog's Eastern Katu page (east1236, ktv) now also lists Phuong/Phuang/Phuong Katu/High Katu among its names. The quoted statement is Costello's for Katu as a whole: her 1991 dictionary covers two Low Katu dialects (An-Diem, Phu-Hoa) and one High Katu dialect (marked hk, ~75% vocabulary correspondence with An-Diem), all in Quang Nam west of Da Nang (page scan). The equation High Katu = Phuong is Glottolog's/Wikipedia's, not Costello's; Glottolog's phg coordinates (16.21N 107.47E) fall in Thua Thien-Hue (Nam Dong), where SIL's Phuong is located. Catalog entry should be coded for Katu (east1236/ktv incl. High Katu) with phuo1238 as Glottolog-identified same variety.
